about: Read by a person for scripts/generate_service_allowlist.py. read_only: an exploit-class template (tag cve, rce, kev...; or severity medium or higher) whose requests were read and only ask what the server volunteers or send a protocol hello, version or status request; the sha256 is the file that was read. refused: read and not allowed on a service port (the reason). restored: a template the content rule or the decode check flags that was read and does not authenticate. A template in none of these that is of the exploit class is left out as not reviewed. frames_read (fifth pass): a template whose hex inputs are binary frames the decode cannot judge; the sha256 is the file whose frames a person decoded and read (see frames_read_notes); a binary-frame template in neither frames_read, read_only nor restored is left out as not read.

smb-signing.reason: The template passes User and Pass to ListSMBv2Metadata, whose signature is (host, port) only (nuclei pkg/js/libs/smb/smb.go; it calls DetectSMBv2, an SMB2 negotiate); the extra arguments are dropped. Measured on nuclei 3.11.1 against a capturing listener: the template sends an SMB2 NEGOTIATE (106 bytes, command 0, dialect 0x0202) and nothing else, no session setup, no NTLMSSP, no user name.

perforce-detection.reason: It emulates the handshake of "p4 info" (func user-info), which Perforce answers without a login; the client field "user" is the placeholder client name, there is no password, ticket or login func (the bytes were captured). It connects to the target port and to 1666, so it is on the list with fixed_ports [1666] and runs only on a target whose port is 1666.

mongodb-unauth.reason: The decode flags the word admin. Read in full: the hex is one OP_MSG (length 69, request id 1, opcode 2013, flags 0, kind 0) with the document {getLog: "startupWarnings", $db: "admin"}; admin is the database name, not an account. getLog startupWarnings is a read of the server log buffer, sent with no login, and no other command, no saslStart, no authenticate, no user name or password is sent. The template has a single input and a single matcher (totalLinesWritten).

mongodb-detect.reason: The decode flags the word admin. The hex is one OP_QUERY (opcode 2004) to the collection admin.$cmd with the document {ismaster: 1}; admin is the database name, not an account. isMaster is the handshake every driver starts with, answered with no login; no saslStart, no authenticate, no user name or password. Read at v10.5.2.

mongodb-info-enum.reason: The decode flags the word admin. The hex is one OP_QUERY (opcode 2004) to the collection admin.$cmd with the document {buildinfo: 1}; admin is the database name, not an account. buildinfo reads the server's version and build, sent with no login, and nothing else is sent. Read at v10.5.2.

ldap-metadata.reason: The decode flags the word anonymous, which is the Realm argument of ldap.Client (the realm, a name for the authentication domain, not an account). The only call after the constructor is CollectMetadata, a read of the rootDSE (the directory's own description of itself), which needs no bind; no Authenticate, no user name and no password is passed. It reaches an optional StartTLS upgrade only. Read at v10.5.2.

rdp-detection.reason: The decode flags the word cookie. The hex is one X.224 connection request in a TPKT frame whose routing cookie is mstshash=test (a load-balancer routing token, not a login) and an RDP negotiation request (8 bytes: the security protocols the client offers). It is the first packet of every RDP connection, sent before any authentication, and the matchers read the server's confirm. Read at v10.5.2.

samba-detect.reason: The decode flags the word ntlm, which is a property it reads from the reply (response.NTLM), not something it sends. The only library call is ConnectSMBInfoMode, an SMB negotiate (no session setup, no NTLMSSP message, no user name), after isPortOpen. Read at v10.5.2.

rtsp-detect.reason: The decode flags the word root. The hex is one OPTIONS request in SIP/2.0 text (OPTIONS sip:nm SIP/2.0 with Via, From, To, Call-ID, CSeq, Max-Forwards, Contact, Accept); root is the value of the From tag, a SIP dialog tag, not an account. OPTIONS asks which methods the server supports and changes nothing. Read at v10.5.2.

nats-server-enum.reason: The decode flags the word auth, which is the auth_required field it reads back from the server's INFO line. It sends one newline over a plain socket (net.Open and Send) and reads what the server volunteers: NATS sends INFO on connect, and the newline draws the error reply. No CONNECT message, so no credential. Read at v10.5.2.

gost-ssh-detect.reason: The decode flags the word auth in a comment and in the script's own checks of the reply. The tcp step sends the client banner SSH-2.0-Nuclei and reads the server's. The javascript step calls ConnectSSHInfoMode, the same call every allowlisted SSH template uses: a handshake and the SSH 'none' method, which carries no password, key or secret, and no session or channel is opened. Read at v10.5.2.

gost-socks5-detect.reason: The decode flags the word auth in a comment and in the script's check of the reply. It sends the three bytes of a SOCKS5 greeting (version 5, one method, method 0x80) and reads the two-byte answer; no username and password sub-negotiation (method 2) is offered, no CONNECT request follows, and the connection is closed. Read at v10.5.2.

apache-rocketmq-broker-unauth.reason: The decode flags the word test. The hex is one length-prefixed JSON request, {code: 105, language: JAVA, opaque: 1, serializeTypeCurrentRPC: JSON, version: 441, extFields: {topic: TEST}}: code 105 is GET_ROUTEINFO_BY_TOPIC, a read of the route of a topic, and TEST is the name of that topic, not an account. It sends no access key, no signature field and no login, writes nothing and creates nothing; a broker that answers it without demanding a signature is the finding. Read at v10.5.2.
